description: Twelfth-round conservative temporal backfill candidates for the remaining clean not_researched military/base rows requested on 2026-06-05. This report is research-only and is not merged into temporal overrides.
scope_notes: Only rows with recommended_action=research_temporal_dates and prior_research_status=not_researched were considered.
Canadian rows were excluded except geonames:6301413 Pelly Island/Nipterk Base; Canadian rows marked previously_candidate or previously_skipped_no_safe_date were not revisited.
Rows marked previously_candidate or previously_skipped_no_safe_date were excluded.
Included source_ids were checked against webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json and were not present there at generation time.

Candidates require an explicit opening, establishment, activation, construction, transfer, closure, decommissioning, or similarly dated operational marker. Current-listing-only evidence was placed in skipped[].

Where a documented year is a predecessor, successor, or documented-by operational marker rather than a formal base-opening date, the rationale explains the identity link and temporal_confidence is downgraded.

candidates.name: Tolemaida Air Base

source_notes.title: Radio Santa Fe - terrenos del Fuerte Militar de Tolemaida
source_notes.note: The report describes Tolemaida as a major Colombian Army base and states that illegal occupation of its lands has persisted since the unit's foundation in 1954.

source_notes.title: Tolemaida Air Base
source_notes.note: The base profile identifies the row as the Colombian Army airfield at Tolemaida.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames row is the Colombian Army airfield within the Tolemaida military complex. The 1954 year is used as the foundation year for the wider military fort/base complex, not a separately sourced runway opening, so confidence is medium.

candidates.name: San Julian Air Base

source_notes.title: GlobalMilitary.net - San Julian Air Base
source_notes.note: The base profile identifies San Julian as a Cuban military installation and notes it as a primary target during the 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion.

candidates.rationale: A safe opening year was not located, but the source provides a dated military-operational marker showing the air base was active by the 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion. Confidence is low because 1961 is a documented-by year rather than a formal establishment date.

candidates.name: Palmahim Airbase

source_notes.title: Missile Test Unit (Israel)
source_notes.note: The unit history states that the test range at what is now Palmachim Airbase was established in 1969.

source_notes.title: NTI - Palmachim
source_notes.note: NTI describes Palmachim Air Base as built during the 1970s as a missile test site and currently stationing IAF helicopters.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames row is the Palmachim/Palmahim Airbase. The 1969 start marks the establishment of the test range at the present airbase location; confidence is medium because later source material describes the air base buildout more generally as a 1970s facility.

candidates.name: Dyess US Army Air Field

source_notes.title: Pacific Wrecks - Roi Airfield (Dyess AAF)
source_notes.note: The airfield history says that during late 1944, under U.S. occupation, fill was added between Roi and Namur, forming Roi-Namur; the site is now known as Dyess Army Air Field.

source_notes.title: Dyess Army Airfield
source_notes.note: The airfield profile identifies Dyess Army Airfield/Freeflight International Airport as the military airfield on Roi-Namur, Kwajalein Atoll.

candidates.rationale: The row matches Dyess Army Airfield on Roi-Namur. The 1944 marker is tied to the U.S. wartime occupation and site formation rather than a formal named-base activation, so confidence is medium.

candidates.name: Air Force Base Bloemspruit

source_notes.title: South African Air Force - 8 Squadron
source_notes.note: The SAAF squadron history states that 8 Squadron was reinstated on 1 January 1951 as a citizen-force element based at Bloemspruit.

source_notes.title: South African Air Force - Air Force Base Bloemspruit
source_notes.note: The SAAF base page identifies Bloemspruit as a current air force base sharing runways with Bloemfontein Airport.

candidates.rationale: The official SAAF material confirms current base identity and a documented SAAF unit based at Bloemspruit in 1951. Confidence is low because this is a documented-by unit-presence marker, not a formal base opening date.

candidates.rationale: The row directly names Fliegerhorst Aigen im Ennstal/Fiala-Fernbrugg. The 1937 start is supported by anniversary/history material; confidence is medium because the available sources summarize the origin rather than giving a precise opening order.

candidates.name: Kasteli

source_notes.title: Hellenic Air Force - 133 Combat Group

source_notes.title: Kasteli Airport
source_notes.note: The airport/base profile states that Kastelli Airbase was established in November 1940 shortly after the onset of World War II in Greece.

candidates.rationale: The row maps to Kasteli Hellenic Air Force Base. The 1940 establishment date is explicit in the airfield profile and is supported by official HAF wartime operational history at Kasteli.

candidates.name: Hatserim Northwest

source_notes.title: Hatzerim Airbase
source_notes.note: The base history states that Hatzerim Airbase was constructed during the 1960s and declared operational on 3 October 1966.

source_notes.title: GlobalMilitary.net - Hatzerim Airbase
source_notes.note: The base profile repeats that Hatzerim became operational on 3 October 1966.

candidates.rationale: The row appears to represent the northwestern portion of Hatzerim Airbase, where training activity is described in the base history. The 1966 operational date is for the whole airbase, so confidence is medium for this sub-feature.

candidates.name: Base Naval Agustin Armario

source_notes.title: Puerto Cabello
source_notes.note: The city history states that Base Naval Agustin Armario in Puerto Cabello was inaugurated in July 1946 and has hosted the Navy Command since 1960.

source_notes.title: Agustin Armario
source_notes.note: The biographical entry says Naval Base No. 1 at Puerto Cabello was assigned the name Contralmirante Agustin Armario by a 22 July 1963 resolution.

candidates.rationale: The row directly names Base Naval Agustin Armario. The 1946 inauguration is used for the base, with the 1963 naming evidence explaining the later Agustin Armario identity.

candidates.name: Philippine Naval Base

source_notes.title: Naval Station Pascual Ledesma
source_notes.note: The station history states that the former U.S. naval facility was officially turned over to the Philippine government on 1 September 1971 and later renamed Naval Station Pascual Ledesma.

source_notes.title: GMA News - DND urged to retain two Navy stations in Sangley Point
source_notes.note: The report identifies Naval Station Pascual Ledesma as one of the Navy stations in Sangley Point and notes the site houses vital Philippine Navy facilities.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames row maps through Wikidata to Naval Station Pascual Ledesma at Cavite/Sangley Point. The 1971 start marks transfer into Philippine government/naval use; confidence is medium because the Pascual Ledesma name was assigned later.

source_notes.title: BOE - Acuartelamiento Alferez Rojas Navarrete security zone

candidates.rationale: The row names the Rabasa military base. The 1924 first-military-installation marker is supported by local historical reporting and the BOE confirms the continuing defense installation identity.

candidates.name: Loran Station

source_notes.title: Loran-History.info - Loran Station South Caicos
source_notes.note: The station history lists construction from 11 February 1958 to 30 September 1959, establishment in July 1959, operational date 3 July 1959, operations ceased 31 December 1980, and disestablishment in January 1981.

source_notes.title: Visit Turks and Caicos Islands - South Caicos U.S. Coast Guard LORAN Station
source_notes.note: The local history page says the station was completed in 1959, ceased operating at the end of 1980, and was officially decommissioned in 1981.

candidates.rationale: The row matches the South Caicos U.S. Coast Guard LORAN station. The source provides explicit operational and decommissioning bounds, so 1959-1981 is a safe interval.
